observed_failure: Turn Up Time has no role for broad brainstorming or targeted cited research. Discovery researchers each do their own ad hoc web search inside a fixed dimension, and nothing is dedicated to resolving named UNKNOWN MUST claims or generating alternative options before architecture.
evidence: 2026-10-10 repository recon: .claude/agents has 17 agents; only the five *-researcher agents and premise-auditor carry WebSearch/WebFetch, and none owns option generation or UNKNOWN-claim resolution.

2026-10-10 registry recon: .claude/capabilities/registry.json has 33 capabilities; the research-adjacent ones are dependency-docs (context7), reference-app-analysis (rea) and code-symbol-analysis (serena). None is web research.
2026-10-10 owner request: add a Perplexity-style research and brainstorm engine to strengthen the workflow's reasoning.
frequency: Structural gap, present in every Tier C discovery; no single failed project has been attributed to it yet.
root_cause: Discovery coverage is organised by dimension (product, frontend, backend, security). Cross-cutting option generation and targeted re-research of named gaps have no owner, so repeat discovery passes re-run whole dimensions instead of answering the specific UNKNOWN claim.
existing_control: premise-auditor returns EVIDENCE_BLOCKED for unresolved MUST claims, and the loop contract restricts repeats to named gaps. The gap is detected, but no role is specialised to close it cheaply.
proposed_change: Project-only pilot: add a read-only research-scout assurance agent to the pilot project's own .claude/ (project registry resolves first). Modes: (1) brainstorm, which returns at least three materially different options with tradeoffs and sources; (2) gap, which takes named UNKNOWN or CONFLICTED MUST claims and returns SUPPORTED/CONFLICTED/UNKNOWN with URL, quote and retrieval date. Engine: the host's built-in web search by default (no extra cost); Perplexity Sonar only after a recorded readiness probe, an owner-approved spend cap and an egress decision. Each pack records the engine actually used. A different-family premise-auditor (Codex when Claude researched) labels the final verdict. Core CLAUDE.md, topology, schemas and the global registry are not changed during the pilot.
expected_effect: Named UNKNOWN MUST claims are resolved in one targeted spawn rather than a full dimension re-run, and alternative options are visible before architecture.
measurement: Per pilot project: count of named UNKNOWN MUST claims entering gap mode versus leaving SUPPORTED or CONFLICTED; citation validity rate as judged by premise-auditor (URL exists, quote present, supports the claim, applies); spawns and wall time spent on discovery repeats compared with the bandia-project-conversations baseline; count of auditor rejections of scout claims.
seeded_failure_eval: Seed A (RED before): a discovery pack with one MUST claim UNKNOWN and no source. Without research-scout, premise-auditor must return EVIDENCE_BLOCKED and the only legal repeat re-runs the owning dimension. GREEN after: one research-scout gap-mode spawn returns the claim as SUPPORTED or CONFLICTED with a verifiable source, and the auditor accepts it. Seed B (must stay RED): a scout pack citing a non-existent URL or a quote absent from the source must be rejected by premise-auditor. Seed C: a pack that omits the engine-used field fails schema or auditor review.
cost: One agent definition and one pilot-project registry entry. Zero extra spend while the built-in search is used; Perplexity Sonar costs about $1 per million tokens plus $5-14 per 1,000 requests (pricing checked 2026-10-10), and only after owner approval.
new_risks: Research volume inflates spawn use without improving decisions; mitigated by gap mode accepting only named claims.
Scout output treated as authoritative; mitigated by keeping premise-auditor as the only evidence verdict.
Paid-API egress of project details; owner approved a $25 prepaid cap (a $50 monthly cap was discussed first), and scout queries exclude secrets and private data.
Same-family bias if Claude both researches and audits; mitigated by assigning the audit to a different model family.
rollback: Delete the pilot project's research-scout agent file and its project-registry entry. No global file changes need reverting.

human_decision.notes: The owner asked to add Perplexity research to the workflow. Promotion policy allows a project pilot on this warrant; a global change needs measured pilot evidence. Later on 2026-10-10 the owner approved Perplexity Sonar spend with a $25 cap enforced as prepaid credit with auto-reload off (a $50 monthly cap was discussed first) and approved sending research queries to Perplexity. Queries must not include secrets, credentials or private personal data. The key is read only from the PERPLEXITY_API_KEY environment variable and is never written to project files.
